name: Me Today Limited
overview: Me Today Limited is a small-cap NZX-listed health and wellbeing brand based in Newmarket, Auckland, selling supplements, skincare and (via a licensed brand) manuka honey products through retail, online and international distributor channels, plus a small third-party agency-services business. The company placed its manuka honey subsidiaries (King Honey) into receivership on 27 July 2025 after failing to sell or refinance the business, and is now a pure-play branded consumer wellness company operating in New Zealand, the USA, China (via a brand-licensing arrangement), Japan, Ireland, the UAE and newly-entered South East Asia. Trading around NZ$0.052/share on 94.5m shares (~NZ$4.9m market cap), it is a micro-cap turnaround story that only returned to positive net assets in the December 2025 half-year, following the King Honey deconsolidation.

business_model.summary: Revenue comes from (1) direct sale of Me Today branded health/wellbeing products (supplements, skincare, herbal liquids) through NZ pharmacy/grocery retail and international distributors/retail partners, net of contra-revenue 'marketing services provided by customers' payments; (2) a China brand-licensing arrangement paying Me Today a percentage of a Chinese partner's Greater China sales; and (3) a small agency-services segment acting as sales agent for other third-party health/wellness brands. Licence-fee income is effectively royalty-like and high-margin but the partner is progressively buying out the underlying China trademark (now 40%), diluting Me Today's long-run economic interest in that market. Core product sales are transactional/repeat retail sales, not subscription-based recurring revenue. Customer base is a mix of B2B (pharmacy chains, distributors, licensee) and end-consumer B2C pull-through; NZ retail is concentrated with a small number of large chains (Chemist Warehouse, Woolworths, Unichem & Life Pharmacies, Bargain Chemist) and the company explicitly calls out reliance on 'its largest retail partner' for shelf-space growth.

revenue_streams.name: Me Today brand - product sales (net of customer marketing contra-revenue)

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B (pharmacy/grocery retail chains, international distributors, one China licensee) and B2C (online direct/trusted retailers)
business_model.geographic_mix: H1-2026 continuing revenue by customer location: New Zealand 56% ($1.435m), USA 22% ($0.551m), China 16% ($0.401m), Rest of World 7% ($0.167m); expanding into Malaysia/SE Asia, Japan, Ireland, UAE

main_competitors: Comvita (manuka honey/wellness, also NZX-listed and also distressed)
large private-label supplement brands sold through the same pharmacy chains
competitive_position.market_position: Sub-scale challenger brand in a highly fragmented, low-barrier supplements/skincare category; no disclosed market share data, but revenue (~$7-8m gross FY26E) is immaterial next to category incumbents

moat_factors.description: Me Today is a young, small NZ brand without the multi-decade heritage of Blackmores/Comvita/Swisse; brand equity is still being built via retail shelf space wins and influencer marketing, not yet a demonstrated pricing-power asset

A large Chinese sports-nutrition company has scaled Me Today product sales in China and now pays a growing royalty (NZD $1.1m for the 12 months to 31 Mar 2026), which is high-margin and capital-light for Me Today - but the same partner is progressively buying out the China trademark (40% now, rights to 50%), meaning Me Today's exposure to its most successful growth market is a shrinking, fee-only claim rather than full equity upside
Consumer supplements/skincare are low switching-cost categories; no subscription lock-in disclosed

Recently expanded shelf space with its 'largest retail partner' (undisclosed name, implying customer concentration) is a real but reversible commercial win, not a structural barrier to entry for competitors

No evidence of manufacturing scale or input-cost advantage; company pays 'marketing services' contra-revenue to retail customers, i.e., it is paying for shelf placement rather than commanding it through pull-through brand demand

weaknesses: No discernible moat: category has low barriers to entry and Me Today is the smaller player against multiple bigger-scale wellness brands
Revenue concentration risk on a single unnamed 'largest' NZ retail partner and a single China licensee
History of capital destruction (manuka honey acquisition for $36m in 2021, subsequently written off via receivership) raises questions about capital allocation discipline
Consistently loss-making since listing - has never turned an annual profit from continuing operations
Reliance on third-party distributors internationally (Malaysia/SE Asia distributor, Japan partner, Ireland via Chemist Warehouse) limits control over execution and margin capture

growth_drivers: International expansion: new SE Asia distributor with a Malaysia launch (nine products shipped, 600+ influencers/resellers at distributor's anniversary event) and planned Thailand/Vietnam entry in 2027

China brand visibility and licence-fee growth: partner has hit revenue thresholds to take 40% of the China trademark, with licence fee income rising to NZD $1.1m for the 12 months to 31 Mar 2026 (from $640k for 9 months to 31 Dec 2025 disclosed in the Feb-2026 announcement) - this is high-margin, no-capex revenue
Shanghai CBME trade show exposure (~100,000 trade buyers) intended to build further China/Asia distribution leads

NZ retail expansion: expanded shelf space (moving to six shelves) with its largest retail partner, scan data showing NZ retail sales up 132% in the 12 months to 18 Feb 2026, and ~20 further new product launches planned in NZ in calendar 2026

New product development across supplements, skincare, herbal liquids and powders (17 new products launched in calendar 2025, plus NMN/Slim Biotic/Black Seed Oil and functional powder launches in early 2026) to broaden basket size per retail door
Ongoing activity in USA, Japan, Ireland and UAE markets alongside the core NZ and China businesses
Removal of the loss-making, capital-intensive King Honey manuka honey business simplifies the model and stops the cash bleed from that segment

business.description: Continuing revenue of only ~$2.55m in H1-2026 (guided ~$7.4m+ gross for FY26) against corporate overhead means the business has not yet proven it can reach breakeven scale
Growth is disproportionately reliant on one unnamed 'largest' NZ retail partner and one China licensee; loss of either would be highly damaging
International growth (Malaysia/SE Asia, Japan, Ireland) is distributor-led, giving Me Today limited control over in-market execution, pricing and inventory management

The 2021 $36m King Honey acquisition was written off via 2025 receivership; management has a mixed record of capital allocation at this company specifically, even if principals have had prior successes elsewhere

business.risk: Progressive loss of China trademark economics
business.description: The China partner can acquire up to 50% of the Greater China trademark as revenue thresholds are met (already at 40%), permanently capping Me Today's long-run upside from its best-performing growth market to a royalty stream

financial.risk: Thin cash buffer against ongoing burn
financial.description: Cash of $2.226m at 31 Dec 2025 against a $0.999m six-month operating cash outflow implies roughly 12-15 months of runway at the current burn rate before requiring fresh funding, absent a step-change in profitability

financial.risk: Out-of-the-money warrants may not be exercised
financial.description: 95.52m warrants (Series 1: 47.26m exercisable 1-30 Oct 2026; Series 2: 47.26m exercisable Oct 2027) at $0.06 strike are the Board's explicitly stated going-concern backstop ('the potential to access future capital investment'), but the shares trade below the $0.06 strike (~$0.052), so Series 1 - the near-term relief valve - is currently out-of-the-money and holders have no economic incentive to exercise unless the price rallies above $0.06 before 30 Oct 2026
$2.25m BNZ CARL facility matures 15 Sept 2028 at a floating rate (5.78% at 31 Dec 2025), secured over all group property; going-concern assumes 'continued support of the BNZ'
95.52m warrants against 94.5m shares on issue represents up to ~100% further dilution if fully exercised, which would also depress any share price recovery (a natural cap near $0.06)

regulatory.risk: Food/supplement and cosmetic regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions
regulatory.description: Operating in NZ, USA, China, Japan, Ireland/EU and UAE requires navigating varied product registration, labelling and health-claim regimes as the company scales into new markets

regulatory.risk: FMC Act / NZX continuous disclosure obligations
regulatory.description: As an FMC reporting entity and NZX-listed issuer, ongoing compliance costs are a drag on a company this small

macro.description: Revenue generated in USD, RMB and other currencies against NZD reporting and NZD cost base creates translation and transaction FX exposure with no disclosed hedging programme
Supplements and skincare are discretionary/semi-discretionary consumer categories that can soften in a weak consumer spending environment

macro.risk: Manuka honey sector distress as a read-through
macro.description: The broader NZ manuka honey sector (Comvita and others) remains under pressure; while Me Today has exited the capital-intensive honey production business, it retains a Manuka Honey product line and the Pure Manuka/Superlife brand asset acquired out of the King Honey liquidation

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global nutraceuticals/supplements and natural skincare categories continue to grow at mid-single-digit rates on wellness and preventative-health trends, with Asia (particularly China's health-conscious middle class) a structural growth pocket - which aligns with Me Today's China licensing push; NZ manuka-honey-adjacent categories remain structurally challenged by oversupply and falling export prices, reinforcing the rationale for exiting bulk honey production
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - discretionary consumer wellness spend can soften in downturns, though health/immunity-oriented products have shown some resilience historically
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct (small floating-rate BNZ facility of $2.25m); moderate indirect via cost of new equity/debt capital given the company's dependence on external funding to sustain the loss-making growth phase
key_input_costs: Contract manufacturing/formulation costs for supplements and skincare
Marketing/influencer spend and retailer trade-marketing payments (contra-revenue)

recent_developments.event: King Honey Holdings Limited and King Honey Limited placed into receivership by their own directors after failing to sell or refinance the manuka honey business; Me Today, having been ring-fenced from the King Honey debt security group in 2024, recognised a one-off non-cash $4.14m accounting gain on deconsolidation and flipped group net assets from negative $2.3m to positive $3.1m in the FY26 first half
Completed pro-rata rights issue (plus director/employee shares) at $0.06/share, raising ~$2.34m gross (~$2.18m net of costs) and taking shares on issue from 54.3m to 94.5m

Bonus issue of 47.26m Series 1 warrants (exercisable 1-30 Oct 2026 at $0.06) and 47.26m Series 2 warrants (exercisable Oct 2027 at $0.06) to all shareholders on a 1-for-2 basis; no consideration paid, quoted on NZX Main Board as MEEWA/MEEWB

H1-2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) results: continuing revenue $2.554m (+19%), continuing loss after tax $0.902m (improved from $1.476m loss), positive working capital of $5.0m, FY26 gross revenue guidance of >$6.5m and EBITDA loss <$1.7m issued for the first time post-King-Honey

China partner exercised notice to take total ownership of the Me Today China trademark to 40% (having reached 20% in Feb-2025); licence fee for the 12 months to 31 Mar 2026 disclosed at NZD $1.1m, materially up on the $640k reported for the nine months to 31 Dec 2025 in Feb-2026
FY26 (year to 30 Jun 2026) guidance raised to gross revenue exceeding $7.4m and EBITDA loss less than $1.6m

Market update: FY26 gross revenue now expected to be HIGHER than the $7.4m May guidance and the EBITDA loss LESS than $1.6m; cited Malaysia distributor launch (600+ influencers/resellers, nine products shipped), Shanghai CBME expo attendance (~100,000 trade buyers), continued NZ shelf-space expansion and ~20 further NZ product launches planned in the current calendar year; audited FY26 results due to NZX before 31 August 2026 (imminent as of this writing)

guidance.as_of: 29 July 2026 market update (ahead of audited FY2026 results due before 31 August 2026)

items.target: Exceeding $7.4m (originally >$6.5m at Feb-2026 half-year, raised to >$7.4m on 7 May 2026, and reaffirmed as tracking HIGHER still on 29 Jul 2026)
items.notes: Guidance has been progressively raised through the year (Feb: >$6.5m; May: >$7.4m; Jul: higher than $7.4m, no new number given) - a rare positive trend for this company, but note 'gross revenue' is before the marketing-services contra-revenue deduction, which ran at ~$698k in H1-2026 alone, so net reported revenue will be materially lower than the headline figure

items.target: Less than $1.6m (originally <$1.7m at Feb-2026, tightened to <$1.6m on 7 May 2026, and reaffirmed as tracking better still on 29 Jul 2026)
items.notes: Improvement trend is consistent quarter to quarter; audited FY26 numbers (due before 31 Aug 2026) will show whether continuing-operations losses are converging toward breakeven

items.metric: China licence fee (12 months to 31 Mar 2026)
items.vs_prior: n/a - first full annual disclosure of this metric
items.notes: Company noted the 9-month figure to 31 Dec 2025 was $640k, implying acceleration in the licence fee run-rate into calendar Q1 2026
Follows 17 new product launches in calendar 2025

guidance.management_commentary: Management (Chairman Grant Baker and CEO Stephen Sinclair) have consistently framed the story around international expansion (SE Asia, China) and NZ shelf-space gains funding a path toward EBITDA breakeven, while emphasising that 'investment is still required in the brand and the distribution network.' The Board's going-concern statement explicitly cites the Series 1/2 warrants and 'the potential to access future capital investment' as part of its 12-month funding plan, alongside continued BNZ support and existing cash - an implicit acknowledgment that further capital raising (dilutive or warrant-funded) is part of the base case, not a tail risk.

bull_case: King Honey receivership removed a chronically loss-making, capital-intensive $14.1m-liability business at no cost to the parent, leaving a smaller but growing, higher-margin branded consumer business with positive net assets ($3.1m) and positive working capital ($5.0m) for the first time in years

China licensing economics are scaling fast and are high-margin/low-capex for Me Today (licence fee run-rate accelerating to an annualised $1.1m+), giving genuine operating leverage even as the partner buys into the underlying trademark

FY26 guidance has been raised twice in a row (revenue up, EBITDA loss down) with a further positive update in July 2026, and continuing-operations losses have nearly halved year-on-year (H1-2026 loss $0.902m vs $1.476m in H1-2025) - a credible, if early, trajectory toward breakeven

Genuine multi-market international optionality (Malaysia/SE Asia launch, Shanghai trade show exposure, Japan, Ireland via Chemist Warehouse, UAE, USA) gives multiple shots on goal for a step-change in scale without Me Today itself carrying manufacturing or inventory risk in most of these markets

Grant Baker, Stephen Sinclair and Michael Kerr have a genuine prior track record of building and monetising NZ consumer brands (42 Below sold for $132m; Trilogy International sold for $211m), which is the qualitative reason the market has historically extended this team credit despite Me Today's own weak results to date
bear_case: This is a story of repeated capital destruction at THIS company specifically: $54.5m of accumulated losses, a $36m manuka honey acquisition (2021) written off via 2025 receivership, and a share count that has nearly doubled in the past year (54.3m to 94.5m) purely to keep the lights on - the Baker/Sinclair track record at other companies has not yet translated into a Me Today success

No discernible competitive moat: a small, young brand competing against well-capitalised, longer-established wellness brands in a low-switching-cost category, reliant on paying retailers for shelf space (marketing-services contra-revenue) rather than commanding it via consumer pull

Cash runway is tight - roughly 12-15 months at the current ~$1m/half-year burn rate against $2.226m cash at 31 Dec 2025 - and the Board's own going-concern disclosure leans on the Series 1/2 warrants as a funding source; but the shares trade below the $0.06 strike, so the Oct-2026 Series 1 window (the near-term relief valve) is currently out-of-the-money and may not deliver the capital the plan assumes

95.52m warrants against 94.5m shares on issue is a structural ~100% dilution overhang that will suppress any share price recovery near the $0.06 strike and signals the company itself expects to need meaningfully more capital

The China trademark arrangement caps Me Today's own long-run upside in its best-performing market (partner already owns 40%, rights to 50%), converting what could have been full equity participation into a shrinking royalty stream - the growth is real but the economics captured by Me Today shareholders are structurally limited
